Olive (docs): FYI I found examples on the function-calling page using the old `tool.invoke` signature. CI unit-snippets in SDK are failing.
Raj (eng): Yep runtime expects `invokeAction({ action: { name, args } })` now. Quick swap.
Kim (devex): Can you paste the canonical JS/Python snippets so I can update the docs?
Raj (eng): JS:
```js
const r = await client.invokeAction({ action: { name: 'notify.send', args: { to: 'user@example.com' } } });
// r.status === 'ok' && r.output.result.id
```
Python:
```py
r = client.invoke_action({ 'action': { 'name': 'notify.send', 'args': { 'to': 'user@example.com' } } })
# r['output']['result']['id']
```
Olive (docs): Also CI linkcheck flagged an anchor to `#function-response` — heading got renamed to "Function response & guardrails"; site generator suggests `#function-response--guardrails`.
ci-bot: link-check(https://docs.redwood.ai/function-calling#function-response) -> 404 anchor not found. suggested: #function-response--guardrails
Raj (eng): One more: update the JSON schema block to mark `output.result` required when status == 'ok', and document that `error` is only present on failures. Add guardrail: "Treat `error` as the canonical failure indicator."
Kim (devex): I'll open a small PR with JS/Python snippets, schema tweak, guardrail note, and the anchor fix. Will ping for review.
Olive (docs): Great — drop the PR link here and I'll run a final linkcheck before merge.
